trust_decision.summary: A redirect hop must not forward caller-supplied sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, Cookie2, Host, Proxy-Connection, Proxy-Authorization, X-API-Key, X-Auth-Token, X-CSRF-Token, X-Session-ID); the decision is made at the header-duplication sink in RedirectFollower#response_call by deleting exact header names from the duplicated hash, and the CaptureCookies middleware that injects Cookie just before that sink is deleted.

landing_point.why: The tree contains exactly one redirect implementation, and these four delete calls are its only header redaction; the advisory's wording ('additional sensitive/risky headers when following redirects') points an engineer straight at this list.

fix_sites.entry_point: The same request composed with Excon::Middleware::CaptureCookies placed before RedirectFollower in the :middlewares list (it writes datum[:headers]['Cookie'] from the response's Set-Cookie, which RedirectFollower then duplicates)
Library load: require 'excon' no longer defines Excon::Middleware::CaptureCookies

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the advisory names headers the caller supplied in canonical spelling (the four pre-existing deletes already worked that way), so a key like 'authorization'/'x-api-key' is the caller's own deviation; and CaptureCookies is an opt-in cookie-jar feature, not redirect redaction, so it looks like someone else's module.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: CaptureCookies replays a cookie set by the first response on the following redirect (its whole purpose, asserted at tests/middlewares/capture_cookies_tests.rb:6-18); any blanket 'delete Cookie on every redirect' — which is what the published fix does — kills it. Keeping same-origin cookie replay while dropping cross-origin cookies is a legitimate behaviour an over-broad fix breaks.

O6_input_shapes: each listed header present or absent (Hash#delete of a missing key is a no-op, so absent headers need no guard)
the whole header entry removed regardless of its value (single String, empty String, or Array of values)
plain Hash request headers and Excon::Headers containers (Excon::Headers#delete removes the raw key only on an exact spelling match, lib/excon/headers.rb:45-48)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Same redirect sink with a header name in non-canonical case/spelling (:headers => {'authorization' => '...'} or {'x-api-key' => '...'}, or Host under a lowercased key). The redaction is exact-string Hash#delete, so the value is still serialised to the redirect target; for Host the caller's spelling survives connection.rb:259/272-273 and the stale value is re-sent because connection.rb:267 uses ||=.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and the fix name headers in canonical spelling, and the four pre-existing deletes were exact-match too, so a lowercased key reads as an unsupported caller input rather than an uncovered route.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; Host half is one file away in lib/excon/connection.rb:259-273

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second hand-rolled sensitive-header list (Utils.redact keeps only Authorization and Proxy-Authorization) used for instrumentation/log output; a maintained REDACTED_HEADERS constant could be shared with the redirect middleware and extended to X-API-Key/X-Auth-Token/X-Session-ID.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The list already exists in the same gem for the same purpose (hiding credentials in a datum copy), so a maintainer extending 'which headers are sensitive' would plausibly extend it there as well.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third Authorization-only redaction that rewrites params[:headers] before logging; a sibling would make it consult the same header list.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It was written independently of Utils.redact and of RedirectFollower, so the duplicated knowledge is already a real maintenance pattern in this repo.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Keep CaptureCookies in our copy but make it origin-aware (replay only when the redirect target has the same scheme/host/port), instead of deleting the middleware as upstream did.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The feature shipped from 0.46.0 (changelog.txt:648) and has rackup-backed tests (tests/rackups/redirecting_with_cookie.ru), so a maintainer would rather guard it than delete a decade-old public middleware.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A case-insensitive header-delete helper (find the key with casecmp?, delete that key) injected next to the existing Host hoisting code and reused by the redirect sink.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The repo already resolves request-header identity with casecmp? here and at lib/excon/middlewares/decompress.rb:11, so centralising it is a natural refactor.
